correctness.rationale: The claimed depth counts the first equality of consecutive synchronous partitions, starting at round zero with one uniquely marked corner. The degree deficit first becomes available at round one; applying the Laplacian k times uses k additional rounds. Its separated path resolvent satisfies both endpoints (after removing the common prefactor, the left endpoint equation reduces to (1-r^q)/(1-r)) and the interior recurrence for z=-r/(1-r)^2. The change of parameter preserves order of vanishing. The cross-multiplied numerator is anti-reciprocal in degree m+n-1; the R initial zero coefficients force all coefficients to vanish except in the four expressly handled small cases. At a primitive q-th root, the reflected-position amplitudes have distinct cosine factors on the near half of the path, so a nonzero difference of reflection types has least period q. Thus the shorter and longer path differences cannot cancel unless both vanish; for squares, coefficient multiplicities distinguish unordered pairs of reflection types. A root-distance d at most R gives a shortest-walk count binom(d,i) with just the swap ambiguity. An unequal swap cannot preserve both rectangle reflection types because it would require i+j=m-1=n-1. Outside radius R, only the far-far position in a reflection orbit remains, modulo swap on a square. The reflected witness in the final column has distances R and greater than R, is indistinguishable before R, and splits at R. Direct small-case refinement gives round depths 1, 2, 2, 3 for (2,2), (2,3), (3,3), (3,4); in the last case round two leaves only the doubletons {(0,3),(2,3)} and {(2,1),(2,2)}, both split by their neighbors in round three. An independent in-memory implementation using retained vertex color and sorted neighbor colors checked depth and orbit partition on 63 pairs, 2<=m<=10 and m<=n<=12. The supplied direct/algebra scripts and recorded outputs were inspected, not executed. The bounded replay corroborates the finite cases; the proof establishes the universal depth.

value.rationale: A single initial marker is a natural individualization of rectangular grids. The exact synchronous depth explains when boundary information and the marker together finish refinement, rather than simply giving eventual identifiability or an order-of-growth bound. The reflected far-column pair certifies a sharp obstruction, and the even/odd short-side dependence is useful when comparing refinement depths across initializations.
